In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the off-axis effect is a real one and that it is not due to the presence of a surface layer.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the off-axis silicon sample is a useful device for the investigation of charge transport phenomena.
the transport properties and space charge densities in a thin offaxis, sample of n-type silicon are not significantly altered by offaxis, crystallographic orientation.
the off-axis sample has transport coefficients which are similar to the corresponding coefficients of the on-axis sample, but the off-axis sample is more sensitive to the presence of space charge.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the space charges in off-axis samples are much more complex and can be very different than the simple picture of space charge in the literature.
off-axis samples are not as simple to model as one might naively think.
